questions.q: Acquired cataract per the book overview is defined as:
opts: Any opacity in the vitreous or its capsule
Any opacity in the lens or its capsule
questions.exp: Any opacity in the lens or its capsule. (Book p73)

questions.q: Fill up: Gradual painless loss of vision → Blindness, m/c cause in ___.
questions.exp: Blindness (m/c cause in India). (Book p73)

questions.q: Which statement about loss of vision in cataract is TRUE per the book's note?
opts: Can be gradual/sudden, painless/pain (signs of inflammation)
questions.exp: Loss of vision: Gradual, sudden; Painless, pain (Signs of inflammation). (Book p73)

questions.q: Match classification per the book — 1) Acquired 2) Congenital … A) Metabolic, Traumatic, Complicated, Senile/age related B) Infantile Onset <1 year, Developmental Onset >1 year C) Only senile
questions.exp: Classification: Acquired: metabolic, traumatic, complicated, senile/age related; Congenital: Infantile (Onset <1 year), Developmental (Onset >1 year). (Book p73)

questions.q: True diabetic cataract/snow flake cataract per the book is:
questions.exp: True diabetic cataract/Snow flake cataract: Cortical cataract, Type 1 DM. (Book p73)

questions.q: Fill up: Pre-senile cataract is m/c in type 2 DM, senile cataract before 50 yrs, D/t ___ of crystallins.
questions.exp: D/t carbamylation of crystallins. (Book p73)

questions.q: All of the following are other ocular conditions due to DM listed in the book EXCEPT:
opts: Fluctuating refractory errors d/t fluctuations in glycemic state
questions.exp: Note Other conditions of eye d/t DM: Fluctuating refractory errors D/t fluctuations in glycemic state, Diabetic retinopathy nonproliferative proliferative; Oil droplet is galactosemia. (Book p73)

questions.q: Oil droplet cataract is described as:
opts: Only reversible cataract, posterior subcapsular, seen in infancy due to galactosemia
Irreversible cortical cataract seen in elderly
Christmas tree cataract due to myotonic dystrophy
questions.exp: Galactosemia: Oil droplet cataract/posterior subcapsular cataract; Only reversible cataract; Seen in infancy. (Book p73)

questions.q: Match galactosemia enzyme deficiency with type — 1) Galactose-1-PUT 2) UDP galactose epimerase 3) Galactokinase … A) Classical galactosemia (grouped) B) Galactose substrate & galactitol/dulcitol accumulate in lens C) Autosomal recessive deficiency listed
questions.exp: D/t autosomal recessive deficiency: Galactose-1-PUT (Phosphate uridyl transferase) + UDP galactose epimerase } Classical galactosemia; Galactokinase: Galactose substrate & galactitol/dulcitol metabolites accumulate in lens. (Book p73)

questions.q: An infant after starting breast milk develops vomiting, cataract described as oil droplet posterior subcapsular, reversible. Urine shows reducing substances. Deficiency likely in galactose-1-PUT (classical galactosemia). This matches the book's description of:
opts: Galactosemia oil droplet cataract only reversible
questions.exp: Oil droplet/posterior subcapsular, only reversible, seen in infancy, D/t galactosemia, diagnosis urine reducing substances after breast feeding. (Book p73)

questions.q: Fill up: Galactosemia diagnosis per the book — Urine assay measurement of increased ___ after breast feeding.
questions.exp: Diagnosis: Urine assay: measurement of increased reducing substances after breast feeding. (Book p74)

questions.q: Myotonic dystrophy cataract per the book:
opts: Christmas tree/posterior subcapsular, scattered fine iridescent irregular opacities
questions.exp: Myotonic dystrophy: Christmas tree cataract/posterior subcapsular cataract; Scattered, fine, iridescent irregular opacities. (Book p74)

questions.q: All are associated ocular manifestations of myotonic dystrophy per the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Associated ocular manifestation: Ptosis, Diplopia; Lens: Christmas tree/posterior subcapsular; Sunflower is Wilson's. (Book p74)

questions.q: Match Wilson's ocular finding with cause — 1) Sunflower cataract 2) KF ring … A) Deposition of copper to Descemet's membrane B) Deposition of cuprous oxide at multiple sites C) Deposition of calcium
questions.exp: Lens: Sunflower cataract D/t deposition of cuprous oxide; Cornea Kayser-Fleischer ring: golden brown ring d/t deposition of copper to descemet's membrane (Not pathognomonic). (Book p74)

questions.q: Which statement about Kayser-Fleischer ring is TRUE per the book?
opts: It is pathognomonic of Wilson's and appears first inferiorly
Golden brown ring d/t copper to Descemet's membrane, not pathognomonic, appears superior → inferior → circumferential, missed d/t eyelid
It is due to iron deposition
questions.exp: KF ring: golden brown d/t copper to Descemet's membrane (Not pathognomonic). Seen in all neurological (basal ganglia Cu), only 50% hepatic, Primary biliary cholangitis, Neonatal hepatitis. Progression superior earliest → inferiorly → circumferential, missed clinically d/t being obscured by eyelid. (Book p74)

questions.q: KF ring is seen in all of the following per the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Seen in: All case neurological involvement (Basal ganglia Cu), Only 50% cases with hepatic involvement, Primary biliary cholangitis, Neonatal hepatitis. (Book p74)

questions.q: Treatment of Wilson's per the book includes chelation and KF ring disappearance:
opts: Penicillamine + Trientine lifelong, Cu load ↓, KF disappears 3-5 years
questions.exp: Chelating agents: Penicillamine and Trientine (Lifelong therapy) MOA Chelation Cu → Cu load ↓ → ↓ Cu absorption KF ring usually disappears after 3-5 years. (Book p74)

questions.q: Which statement about galactokinase deficiency is TRUE per the book?
opts: Galactose substrate & galactitol/dulcitol accumulate in lens → cataract
Galactose is converted to glucose normally
questions.exp: Galactokinase: Galactose (Substrate) & galactitol/dulcitol (metabolites) accumulate in lens resulting in cataract. (Book p74)

questions.q: Per the book, KF ring disappears after chelation therapy in:
questions.exp: KF ring usually disappears after 3-5 years. (Book p74)

questions.q: Fill up: Maintenance therapy Zinc acetate forms zinc copper complex → ↓ ___ absorption.
questions.exp: Maintenance therapy: Zinc acetate (Zinc copper complex → ↓ Cu absorption). (Book p75)

questions.q: Match parathyroid tetany cataract by age — 1) Children 2) Adults … A) Origin Congenital, location Lamellar B) Origin Acquired, location Subcapsular C) Origin Traumatic, location Cortical
questions.exp: Parathyroid tetany Leads to hypocalcemia → Cataract: Children Origin Congenital location Lamellar; Adults Origin Acquired location Subcapsular. (Book p75)

questions.q: Blunt trauma cataract per the book is:
questions.exp: Blunt trauma: Rosette shaped cataract: Posterior subcapsular. (Book p75)

questions.q: All of the following traumatic cataract associations are listed EXCEPT:
opts: Infrared: Highest wavelength, Glassblower's cataract True exfoliation of lens capsule
Penetrating: Iron deposition Siderosis bulbi d/t trauma with iron objects Cortical cataract
questions.exp: Blunt: Rosette posterior subcapsular; Lightning: Anterior capsular; Infrared: Highest wavelength Glassblower's cataract True exfoliation; Penetrating: Siderosis bulbi cortical. Sunflower is Wilson. (Book p75)

questions.q: Fill up: Glassblower's cataract due to infrared rays (highest wavelength) is true exfoliation of ___.
questions.exp: Infrared rays: Highest wavelength rays, Glassblower's cataract (True exfoliation of lens capsule). (Book p75)

questions.q: A worker with penetrating injury from iron hammer develops brownish deposits in lens and iris, cortical cataract. Per the book this is:
opts: Siderosis bulbi due to iron deposition d/t trauma with iron objects
Sunflower cataract due to cuprous oxide
questions.exp: Penetrating trauma: Iron deposition in eye: Siderosis bulbi (D/t trauma with iron objects) Cortical cataract. (Book p75)

questions.q: Complicated cataract per the book is:
opts: Posterior subcapsular cataract caused secondary to another condition
Anterior subcapsular due to trauma only
Nuclear cataract due to age only
questions.exp: Posterior subcapsular cataract caused secondary to another condition. (Book p75)

questions.q: Fill up: Mnemonic UMAR for complicated cataract — Uveitis (m/c), High myopia, Angle closure glaucoma, ___.
questions.exp: Mnemonic UMAR: Uveitis (m/c), High myopia, Angle closure glaucoma, Retinitis pigmentosa: Pigment deposition in retina along with night blindness. (Book p75)

questions.q: Appearance of complicated cataract per the book is:
opts: Oil droplet appearance with posterior subcapsular location
Sunflower cataract with cuprous oxide deposition
Rosette shaped posterior subcapsular cataract after blunt trauma
questions.exp: Appearance: Breadcrumbs with polychromatic lustre. (Book p75)
